Online Return

SMSF annual return and audit

A self-managed super fund lodges one annual return that combines its income tax return, regulatory information and member contributions. Before it can be lodged, the fund’s accounts must be audited by an approved SMSF auditor who is independent of the fund and of whoever prepared the accounts. We prepare everything and arrange the audit.

Our fee

from $1,099 + $499 audit inc. GST

Fixed for the accounts and return, with the independent audit fee shown separately.

ATO levy

$259 a year

Paid with the return. A newly registered fund pays two years’ levy with its first return.

Who does it

A registered tax agent

BRS Advisory Pty Ltd, Registered Tax Agent, CPA Australia Public Practice. Every client ID-verified before work starts.

What’s included

  • Fund financial statements and member statements
  • Contributions checked against each member’s caps
  • Pension minimums and transfer balance reporting checked
  • Actuarial certificate arranged where the fund pays pensions
  • Independent audit by an approved SMSF auditor
  • SMSF annual return prepared and lodged

How it runs

  1. 01 Verify identity online — each director, trustee or controlling owner does a three-minute check on their phone, included in the fee. Every client, every service, no exceptions. How it works.
  2. 02 Send bank and investment statements, and market values at 30 June.
  3. 03 We prepare the accounts and flag any compliance concerns before the auditor sees them.
  4. 04 The independent auditor completes the financial and compliance audit.
  5. 05 Trustees sign off, and we lodge the return with the levy.

How an SMSF is taxed

A complying fund generally pays 15% tax on its assessable income, including concessional contributions and earnings, with a one-third discount on capital gains on assets held for more than 12 months. Earnings on assets supporting retirement-phase pensions are generally exempt, which is why pension reporting has to be right. Some income, such as non-arm’s length income, is taxed at the top rate.

When the return is due

A newly registered fund’s first return has its own due date, which is earlier than later years. After that, due dates depend on the fund’s lodgement history. Funds lodging through a registered agent usually have more time. The audit has to be finished before lodgement, so we don’t leave it to the last month.

The audit isn’t a formality

The auditor checks the accounts and whether the trustees followed super law. Typical issues are loans to members, assets not held in the fund’s name, and investments that don’t meet the sole purpose test. The auditor must report serious breaches to the ATO. We’d rather find those issues while preparing the accounts, when they can often still be fixed.

We prepare the fund’s accounts, audit arrangements and tax return. We don’t advise on which investments the fund should hold.
